He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma Sooners]] and is the older brother of [[Blake Griffin]]. ==Early years== Taylor Griffin was born on April 18, 1986, in [[Oklahoma City]], [[Oklahoma]], to Tommy Griffin, who is of [[Haitians|Haitian]] descent,{{cite web|url=http://csmsmagazine.org/?p=6483 |title=Blake Griffin: no longer a rookie |accessdate=13 March 2014}}{{cite web|url=https://www.bet.com/photo-gallery/twz7im/one-drop-rule-a-guide-to-black-celebs/9u1q0o |title=One drop rule:A guide to black celebrities |website=[[BET]] |access-date=13 March 2014}} and to Gail Griffin, who is white.[http://www.soonersports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/griffin_taylor00.html Taylor Griffin – SoonerSports.com] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110124053052/http://www.soonersports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/griffin_taylor00.html |date=2011-01-24 }}. soonersports.com. Retrieved January 3, 2011. Retrieved January 4, 2011. Blake and Taylor Griffin played at [[Oklahoma Christian School]] under their father, who was the head coach. The brothers played together during the 2003–04 and 2004–05 high school seasons, winning two Oklahoma 2A state high school basketball championships. Considered a three-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Griffin was listed as the No. 34 power forward and the No. 141 player in the nation in 2005.[https://rivals.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Taylor-Griffin-28938;_ylt=AomxdbKLmbqU7RCEnJXdtgPXO5B4 Taylor Griffin Recruiting Profile] ==College career== With his brother Blake, Taylor Griffin helped lead Oklahoma to the Elite Eight of the 2009 NCAA men's basketball tournament. As a senior, he averaged 9.6 points, 5.8 rebounds, and 1.3 steals a game with 53.6% field goal shooting, and 35.7% three-point field goal shooting.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/griffta01.html Taylor Griffin NBA & ABA Stats] ==Professional career== === Phoenix Suns (2009–2010) === Griffin was selected by the [[Phoenix Suns]] with the 48th overall pick of the [[2009 NBA draft]].[http://www.crimsonandcreammachine.com/2009/6/25/925700/blake-griffin-goes-1-taylor Blake Griffin Goes #1; Taylor Griffin Just Drafted #48 By Suns] His younger brother [[Blake Griffin|Blake]] was taken as the [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|1st pick]] by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. He joined the Suns for the 2009 NBA Summer League. On August 17, 2009, he signed his first professional contract with the Suns.[http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Taylor_Griffin/Summary/1685 Taylor Griffin Player Profile – RealGM] Griffin was assigned multiple times to the [[Iowa Energy]] during his rookie season.[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=5689 Suns assign Taylor Griffin to D-League] Griffin re-joined the Suns for the 2010 NBA Summer League. On July 26, 2010, he was waived by the Suns. === Belgacom Liège Basket (2010–2011) === In August 2010, Griffin signed with [[Liège Basket|Belgacom Liège Basket]] of [[Basketball League Belgium Division I|Belgium]].[http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/belgium/12133/belgacom_liege_adds_taylor_griffin_and_cedric_bozeman.html Belgacom Liege adds Taylor Griffin and Cedric Bozeman] === Dakota Wizards (2012) === On December 10, 2011, Griffin signed with the [[Charlotte Bobcats]]. However, he was waived by the Bobcats on December 23. On January 9, 2012, he was acquired by the [[Dakota Wizards]].{{cite web|url=http://bismarcktribune.com/sports/basketball/professional/dleague/wizards/wizards-dakota-signs-taylor-griffin/article_1981e858-3b3d-11e1-8466-0019bb2963f4.html|title=WIZARDS: Dakota signs Taylor Griffin|work=BismarckTribune.com|date=January 9, 2012|accessdate=November 18, 2013}} === Santa Cruz Warriors (2012–2015) === In November 2012, Griffin was acquired by the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]]. In November 2013, he was reacquired by the Warriors.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/santacruz/warriors_training_camp_roster_1314.html Santa Cruz Warriors Announce Training Camp Roster] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150408235135/http://www.nba.com/dleague/santacruz/warriors_training_camp_roster_1314.html |date=2015-04-08 }} On January 3, 2014, he was waived by the Warriors due to a season-ending injury. On November 3, 2014, he was again reacquired by the Warriors.{{cite news|title=Santa Cruz Warriors Announce 2014 Training Camp Roster|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/santacruz/warriors_training_camp_roster_110314.html|accessdate=November 11, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=November 3, 2015, he won the D-League championship with the Warriors.{{cite news|title=Title Wave: Santa Cruz Wins NBA D-League Championship|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20150426/FWNSCW/|accessdate=April 26,
